thread:
Anya: quick callout — after running quantized evals on the rtx cluster, BERTScore jumped ~0.06 vs fp16 but EM and pass@k stayed the same. suspicious.
Mike: can you drop the CI eval log/snippet?
Anya: pasted snippet:
```
Eval: model=llama-3q-8bit seed=42
metrics: { exact_match: 0.61, pass@5: 0.87, bleu: 0.34, bertscore: 0.79 }
```
Local fp16 run (same preds) gives bertscore 0.73.
Sophia: tokenization differences often explain BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore deltas. Which tokenizer/version did the CI image use?
Anya: CI uses eval-harness:latest built by eng-ml/ci. requirements pinned loosely; suspect bertscore or transformers wheel differs between builder and local env.
Rahul: also check sentencepiece vs tokenizer_fast and normalization flags. tiny unicode normalizations change BERTScore.
Mike: FYI pass@k had a subtle bug: duplicates counted as separate samples in our previous impl — inflated pass@k if model returns duplicate candidates.
Anya: we merged a PR that changed unique counting. Example: if model returns the identical string 3x, it was treated as 3 distinct successes. filed ENGML-922.
Sophia: best practice: dedupe per-example candidate set before computing pass@k. math note:
```
# pass@k expected for n samples with m correct: 1 - comb(n-m, k)/comb(n, k)
# in practice dedupe identical candidates then compute.
```
Rahul: proposed CI fixes:
- pin tokenizers/sentencepiece in builder image
- add a smoke check comparing embedding cosines vs a stored baseline
- unit tests asserting pass@k behavior on toy cases (duplicates)
Mike: I'll open PR to pin tokenizers==0.13.3 and sentencepiece==0.1.98 in the builder image.
ci-bot: build #782 failed — test eval_harness::bertscore_consistency flaky on rtx-pool, rerun?
Anya: rerun didn't help; quantized runner still shows variance.
Sophia: another angle: BERTScore depends on the reference embedding model (roberta-large by default). If CI cached a different HF model/version that would shift scores.
Anya: harness has bertscore>=0.3.13 in requirements; that can pull different transformer weights across builds.
Rahul: action items:
- Mike: pin tokenizers/sentencepiece + add smoke e2e with cosine check (ETA 1d)
- Sophia: pin and checksum the bertscore reference model in CI, add assert (ETA 2d)
- Anya: revert the pass@k uniqueness change and add tests for duplicates (ETA today)
- Rahul: build a small reliability-diagram util for calibration (ECE + plots) and hook to dashboard (ETA 3d)
Sophia: ECE quick: bucket predictions and compute sum(|acc - conf| * weight). Will add unit tests with synthetic logits.
Mike: suggestion: attach env artifacts (pip-freeze, python version) to every eval run to make diffs easier.
Anya: adding env.txt artifact sounds good — helped before.
Mike: opened PR #4187 pinning tokenizers in builder; CI queued.
Eval-bot: quick-eval run: https://eval.redwood.internal/runs/2026-03-14/8842 — contains preds, metrics, env artifacts.
Rahul: for dashboards we should show metric deltas across runner variants (fp16 vs quant vs cpu) with dataset and seed filters. will add to grafana/eval dashboard.
Anya: mitigation: mark BERTScore as informational for alerts until we have deterministic pipeline.
Sophia: also adding docs note: "BERTScore can vary across builds; pin deps and reference model for reproducible results." will PR docs.
Mike: added unit tests for pass@k duplicates (tests/test_passk.py) — local CI green.
Anya: reverted #4123 and opened follow-up PR with tests #4192.
Rahul: once PRs merge I'll run a full matrix eval across fp16/8bit/int8 to validate.
Mike: tagging @eng-oncall since eval jobs might use quota.
Anya: thanks all — closing this thread unless more anomalies appear.
